unit.title: Kindness, the Golden Temple, and Prayer

lesson.title: Seva and Kindness in Everyday Life
lesson.subject: sikhi

contentBlocks.text: Last year you learned that Seva means helping others without expecting anything back. This year let's go deeper: what does Seva look like as real, everyday kindness?

Kindness is Seva in action — small, real choices that help someone else feel cared for. Sharing your snack with a friend who forgot theirs, helping a sibling pick up spilled toys, or comforting someone who's sad are all real acts of kindness. The key is doing it because you care, not because you want a reward or praise. Think of one act of kindness you did this week, or one you could do today.
Every act of kindness, no matter how small, is real Seva. This week, keep watching for chances to practice it.

objectives: Connect Seva (from last year) to concrete, everyday acts of kindness
Identify and describe one real act of kindness the child has done or could do
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review what Seva means from last year.
2. Introduce kindness as Seva in action — small, real, caring choices.
3. Brainstorm 3-4 examples of kindness together (sharing, helping, comforting).
4. Ask the child to describe a real act of kindness they've done or could do soon.
5. Move to the worksheet: write or draw about that act of kindness.
6. Close by picking one specific act of kindness to practice this week.
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just one concrete example (sharing) rather than brainstorming many kinds of kindness at once
Ready for more: discuss how kindness sometimes takes courage (like standing up for someone) as well as gentleness
For a child who enjoys stories, read or tell a short story about a character choosing kindness
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is an open-ended, personal reflection activity — there is no single right/wrong answer.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Deepening last year's Seva introduction into concrete, everyday kindness is the Grade 1 Sikhi course's stated starting point, building real understanding before the week moves into the Golden Temple and prayer.
